detail: Known: EIA's 2025 averages, residential 17.30 and industrial 8.62 cents a kWh (EIA Electric Power Monthly table 5.6.A, https://www.eia.gov/electricity/monthly/epm_table_grapher.php?t=epmt_5_6_a), a gap of 86.8 USD per MWh against ours of 87.7; Berkeley Lab's Retail Price Trends, 2026 edition (https://eta-publications.lbl.gov/sites/default/files/2026-07/retail_price_trends_2026_edition_julyupdate.pdf), describes the gap widening. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: the figure is EIA's own net interstate receipts series for Pennsylvania (Natural Gas Annual, table S40, https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/Annual/pdf/table_S40.pdf, gives the 2024 interstate deliveries of 5,891 Bcf); the draft repeats EIA's own series. Seen in search results, page not opened.

New as far as found: no publisher found printing the yearly mean of Gulf Coast gasoline spot less WTI; EIA's Today in Energy prints New York Harbor gasoline crack spreads (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=66964) and RBN Energy the Gulf Coast 3-2-1 spread (https://rbnenergy.com/daily-posts/analyst-insight/usgc-3-2-1-crack-spread-cools-remains-strong), both other measures. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: TVA's own statements, reported by the American Public Power Association (https://www.publicpower.org/periodical/article/tva-sets-new-all-time-power-demand-record-power-system-remains-stable, January 2025) and Power Engineering (https://www.power-eng.com/business/historic-gas-build-drives-tvas-strategy-as-utility-sets-new-load-records/), give a winter peak hour of 35,319 MW on 22 January 2025 (later 35,430 MW) against a summer peak of 32,318 MW in August 2025. Ours adds the ratio of the five highest winter days to the five highest summer days, by year since 2019 (113.9 percent in 2025). Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: the figure is the Census Bureau's own published revenue of data processing and hosting firms (NAICS 518); FRED (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/REVEF518ALLEST) carries the Service Annual Survey series (310.7 billion USD for 2022). The draft repeats the publisher's own total. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=66704, November 2025) gives CAISO batteries at 4.9 GW on average from 5 to 9 PM in May and June 2025 and gas generation down 18 percent from 2020; no publisher found printing gas's share of 5 to 10 PM generation by year. One search result (Grid Status and EIA notes) says CAISO changed how it collects natural gas output in December 2023, so the 2019 and 2025 figures may not be comparable: this would make the draft wrong. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: the California Public Utilities Commission's resource tracking data, December 2025 release (https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/-/media/cpuc-website/divisions/energy-division/documents/summer-2021-reliability/tracking-energy-development/resource-tracking-data-december-2025-release.pdf), lists 15,762 MW of battery projects online, from CAISO's Master Generating Capability List; Modo Energy (https://modoenergy.com/research/caiso-battery-fleet-2025-q4-15gw-interconnection-queue-standalone-colocated, 24 March 2026) gives 15.7 GW. Ours: 15,777 MW. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known: EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67205, 2026) gives 43.6 GW of operating battery storage at the end of 2025 and 15 GW added in 2025. Ours: 43,678 MW. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known in part: Ascend Analytics (https://www.ascendanalytics.com/blog/emerging-energy-reliability-risks-and-needs-in-ercot-its-not-an-afternoon-problem-anymore) and Grid Status (https://blog.gridstatus.io/ercot-record-july-2026/) describe ERCOT's tightest hours moving to the evening when solar has faded; no publisher found printing solar's output in the tightest hours as a share of capacity. Ours adds the figure by year, 71.1 percent in 2019 against 5.0 percent in 2025. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

Known in part: EIA's Today in Energy (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=66464, October 2025) gives ERCOT solar at 24 GW on average from noon to 1 PM in summer 2025 against 12 GW in summer 2023, and gas's midday share falling from 50 to 37 percent; no publisher found printing solar's share of 11 AM to 4 PM generation by year. Ours adds 32.4 percent in 2025 against 2.5 percent in 2019. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: Berkeley Lab's Queued Up, 2026 edition (https://eta-publications.lbl.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/queued_up_2026_edition.pdf), prints the median months from request to commercial operation by year (61 months for projects built in 2025, all types) and by type; the draft reads Berkeley Lab's own queue data, so it repeats the publisher's measure. Seen in search results, page not opened.

Known: the California Air Resources Board's Monthly LCFS Credit Transfer Activity, September 2026 (https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/September%202026%20-%20Monthly%20LCFS%20Credit%20Transfer%20Activity.pdf), gives a calendar 2025 average of 60 USD a credit (volume weighted); ours, the mean of weekly prices, is 59.26 USD. Seen in search results, page not opened.
